title: Switch to pure-Go SQLite and build without CGO
description: mattn/go-sqlite3 forces CGO, a C toolchain in the build image, and makes cross-compiling release binaries awkward. Switch to modernc.org/sqlite (and golang-migrate's matching driver). Check the points where behaviour can differ: the connection string and pragmas (foreign keys are enabled in internal/database/database.go:57; WAL; busy timeout), date/time scanning, boolean handling, error types used for constraint detection, and anything relying on sqlite_omit_load_extension. Measure the slowest pages before and after. If an unresolvable incompatibility appears, stop and report rather than working around it.

recommended_model.name: Opus 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: A driver swap under the whole application; needs methodical verification of subtle behavioural differences.

acceptance_criteria: CGO_ENABLED=0 builds succeed for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64
Unit, e2e, multi-club and fresh-install suites pass on the new driver
A copy of a real production database opens, migrates and serves correctly (Jim provides the copy; it stays local)
Foreign keys, WAL and a busy timeout are confirmed active by a startup self-check
Timings for dashboard, planning matrix and team selection are recorded before and after; no page regresses by more than an agreed margin
The Docker build no longer installs gcc, musl-dev or sqlite-dev; the runtime image no longer needs sqlite-libs

files_to_modify: Makefile (test targets no longer need CGO)
notes: Driver name changes from 'sqlite3' to 'sqlite'; DSN pragma syntax differs (_pragma=foreign_keys(1)).
Verify details against the modernc.org/sqlite and golang-migrate documentation rather than memory.

testing_requirements: Manual check against a production database copy

context.user_story: As the maintainer, I want release binaries for more than one architecture without a C toolchain.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
